chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

While the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was in al-Masjid al-Haram and he was wearing new clothes, the polytheists threw the stomach contents of a she-camel upon him, filling his clothes with it. That affected him as Allah willed. Then he went to Abū Ṭālib and said to him, “O my uncle, how do you regard my standing among you?” He said to him, “What is that, O son of my brother?” So he informed him of the matter.

Then Abū Ṭālib called Ḥamzah, took the sword, and said to Ḥamzah, “Take the stomach contents.” Then he headed toward the people, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was with him. He came to Quraysh while they were around the Kaʿbah, and when they saw him, they recognized anger in his face. Then he said to Ḥamzah, “Smear the stomach contents upon their moustaches.” So he did that until he had reached the last of them.
Then Abū Ṭālib turned to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said, “O son of my brother, this is your standing among us.”

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaʿbah, around which Quraysh were gathered
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ: the Sacred Mosque in Mecca, the setting of the incident
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكُونَ: the polytheists who committed the insult against the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.حَسَبِي: my standing, lineage, or noble regard among my people
key_terms.سَلَى نَاقَةٍ: the stomach contents or afterbirth of a she-camel thrown upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.سِبَالِهِمْ: their moustaches, upon which the filth was smeared
key_terms.قُرَيْشًا: the Quraysh, the Meccan tribe gathered around the Kaʿbah

ai.seo_question: How did Abū Ṭālib respond when Quraysh humiliated the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله in al-Masjid al-Haram?
ai.summary: This narration recounts an incident in which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was insulted by the polytheists in al-Masjid al-Haram, after which he informed Abū Ṭālib of what had happened. Abū Ṭālib responded decisively, confronting Quraysh and demonstrating his protection and support for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. The report highlights the hostility of the مشرکون and the familial defense extended to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله in the early Meccan period.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘While the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was in the Sacred Masjid and upon him<sup>saww</sup> were new clothes, so the Polytheists threw upon him<sup>saww</sup> the stomach contents of a she-camel. So his<sup>saww</sup> clothes were stained by it. So there entered into him<sup>saww</sup> due to that, whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desired. So he<sup>saww</sup> went to Abu Talib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> and said to him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>: ‘O Uncle! How do you<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> view my<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> nobility among you all?’ So he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> said to him<sup>saww</sup>: ‘And what is that, O son<sup>saww</sup> of my<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> brother<sup>as</sup>?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> informed him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> the news.

So Abu Talib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> called Hamza<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> and grabbed the sword and said to Hamza<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> to take the stomach contents (of a camel), then divert towards the group, and the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was with him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>. So he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> came to the Qureysh, and they were around the Kabah. So when they saw him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>, they recognised the ferocity in his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> face. Then he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> said to Hamza<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>: ‘Paste the stomach contents (of a camel) upon their faces’. So he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> did that until he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> came to their last one.

Then Abu Talib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> turned towards the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> said: ‘O son<sup>saww</sup> of my<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> brother<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>! This is your<sup>saww</sup> nobility among us’.
en.sarwar: 29. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya have narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi from Ishaq ibn Ja‘far from his father (a.s.) who has said the following. “They think that abu Talib was an unbeliever. They speak lies, how could he be an unbeliever when he would say such worlds as herein below.
“Do they not know that we found Muhammad as a prophet like Musa (Moses) whose name is written in the ancient books.”

In another hadith he has said, “How could abu Talib be an unbeliever when he would say, “They certainly know that our child is not a liar to us and the false words are not paid any attention to. The (beautiful) white face that prays for rain from the clouds, is the helper of the orphans and the protector of the widows.”
